rules.note: 4th character is the holder type: A AOP, B BOI, C company, F firm or LLP, G government, H HUF, J artificial juridical person, L local authority, P individual, T trust. No public checksum on the 10th character. SPEC §1.10. Not in the open UNVERIFIED list.
TAN shape required for a TDS GSTIN body. SPEC §1.1 and §1.10.

Opened 2026-11-01. The 4th character is the holder status. The 5th character is the surname or name initial and is not checked. SPEC §1.10 says G is government; the department page says Government Agency.
The department calls the 10th character an alphabetic check digit and does not publish the algorithm. This skill does not check it. SPEC §1.10 says not to claim a public checksum.

Opened 2026-11-01. First 3 letters are the jurisdiction code, the 4th is the name initial, the next 5 digits are the serial (00001 to 99999 on the illustrative example), and the 10th is a check digit.
The department calls the 10th character an alphabetic check digit and does not publish the algorithm. This skill does not check it.

RBI NEFT FAQ updated 2024-09-02, question 4, opened 2026-11-01. 11 characters: first 4 letters are the bank, the 5th character is 0, the last 6 are the branch. The FAQ calls it an 11-digit code; the branch characters are alphanumeric in SPEC §1.10.
Same NEFT FAQ. The reserved 5th character is 0.

rules.value: Format valid does not mean the branch participates in NEFT or RTGS.
rules.note: The FAQ says an IFSC identifies a branch participating in NEFT. A pattern match is not that list. The RBI list is at https://rbi.org.in/Scripts/bs_viewcontent.aspx?Id=2009 and this skill does not call it.
SPEC §1.10 names this host for an opt-in lookup. It is not the RBI branch list. UNVERIFIED as proof that a branch is active.
SPEC §1.10. The MasterCodes pincode table opened 2026-11-01 lists first-3-digit prefixes from 110 to 855, so a leading 0 is outside that table. The 6-digit length is the India Post PIN.

UNVERIFIED. A direct fetch of the India Post PIN page returned HTTP 504 on 2026-11-01. A search index of that page showed Northern, Western, Southern, Eastern, and Army Postal Service. SPEC §1.10 shortens the first four to North, West, South, and East.

Pincode State Mapping Pattern opened 2026-11-01. Display names are title case of that table. Code 26 is Dadra and Nagar Haveli there, and it lists both 362 and 396. 396 is also on 24 and 25. 403 is inside Maharashtra 400-445 and is also Goa. A mismatch is only a warning.
TRAI consultation on the National Numbering Plan, 6 Jun 2024, opened 2026-11-01. It describes a country code plus a 10-digit national number. The paper's own contact line uses +91.
The same paper says dialling prefix 0 is mandatory for a fixed-to-mobile call, and that all 10 national digits are dialled for a mobile-to-mobile call.
National significant number length for cellular mobile is 10 digits.

UNVERIFIED as a complete DoT rule. TRAI's 29 May 2020 recommendations, opened 2026-11-01, say DoT had allocated level 9, level 8, level 7, and some sub-levels of level 6 for mobile. Level 6 is partial, and later recommendations discuss levels 2, 3, and 4. SPEC §1.10 says to mark this pattern verified false.

UNVERIFIED. SPEC §1.10 says to reject toll-free 1800. The 2003 National Numbering Plan PDF opened 2026-11-01 moves IN service codes to 18XX and does not itself say that every 1800 number is toll-free.
Section 3(4), as inserted by Act 14 of 2019 with effect from 25 Jul 2019. The number is twelve digits. Section 4(2) says it is random and bears no relation to the holder's attributes.
UIDAI dos and don'ts for requesting entities, 31 Oct 2022. Do not keep a copy of an Aadhaar letter without masking the first 8 digits. Show the last 4 only, as XXXX XXXX 1234.

UNVERIFIED. A leading 0 or 1 is a common implementation check. UIDAI does not publish it. Section 4(2) says the number bears no relation to attributes. Warn only. Do not reject on it alone. 999999999999 starts with 9 and does not trip it.

rules.value: Verhoeff valid does not mean UIDAI issued this number.
rules.note: Section 3(3): the Authority issues the number after verification. A checksum is not that issuance.

rules.value: Section 29 restricts sharing. Core biometric information must not be shared, and must not be used except to generate Aadhaar numbers and to authenticate. Other identity information may be shared only as the Act and regulations allow. A requesting entity or offline verification-seeking entity may use or disclose identity information only for the purposes told to the person in writing, in clear language. An Aadhaar number, demographic information, or photograph must not be published or displayed publicly except as regulations allow.
rules.note: Opened 2026-11-01. Sub-sections (3) and (4) are the text substituted by Act 14 of 2019, section 13, with effect from 25 Jul 2019. This is not a complete restatement of the Act.

rules.value: Requesting entities must store Aadhaar numbers and connected Aadhaar data, such as eKYC XML, only in an Aadhaar Data Vault. Other systems keep a reference key. The Aadhaar number must not be recoverable from that key, and hashing the Aadhaar number is not allowed as the key.
rules.note: UIDAI Circular No. 14 of 2025, 4 Nov 2025, opened 2026-11-01. It supersedes the 25 Jul 2017 vault circular and Circular 8 of 2025. SPEC §1.11 said to mark vault details verified false because the site was flaky; this circular was opened, so the storage rule is verified. Hosting choices such as GCC and HSM are in the circular and are not copied into this value.

UIDAI FAQ: a Virtual ID is a temporary, revocable 16-digit number mapped to the Aadhaar number. The FAQ does not state a launch date; 2018-07-01 is only so the row is in force on the as-of date. There is no published checksum in that FAQ.
UNVERIFIED. The 12-digit mask redacts the first 8 digits. This row extends that display to a 16-digit VID. The UIDAI VID FAQ does not publish a mask template.

rules.value: Do not store a Virtual ID. UIDAI says it is temporary, the holder can replace it, and storing it has no value.
rules.note: UIDAI FAQ answer to whether an agency can store a VID: No.
